recipes.name: Baked Chicken with Peaches
ingredients_raw: 4 fresh peaches - peeled, pitted, and sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Place chicken in the prepared baking dish; sprinkle with ½ cup brown sugar. Arrange peach slices over chicken; sprinkle with remaining ½ cup brown sugar, lemon juice, ginger, and cloves.
Bake in the preheated oven, frequently basting with juices, until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Chicken with Peaches
raw_recipe.description: This baked chicken with peaches recipe combines the sweetness of peaches and brown sugar with the spice of ginger and cloves, for a dish full of flavor.

review.reviewBody: Don't let some of the reviews scare you away from trying this wonderful recipe! I almost didn't make this because of many reviews complaining about "the sweetness". I'm glad I did! I started by seasoning my chicken breasts with some white wine vinegar and lemon juice. I used the vinegar to offset the sweetness "problem". I then sprinkled black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder over the breasts. I pretty much followed the rest of the recipe as written. I used a fresh peach(with white flesh though) and used a "light" brown sugar to save calories. For the sauce, I used a combo of half cold water/half chilled white wine(Pinot Grigio) mixed with the corn starch. I sprinkled a bit of fresh parsley leaves over it all too. The end result was just fantastic, and even my boyfriend said he couldn't wait until I made this tasty dish again! And, the whole recipe was very quick and easy too. What more could I ask for? Try this, you'll love it! Thank you Lor for a delicious recipe!

I made a few changes, but it turned out delicious! I was cooking for two people, so only used 2 chicken breasts. I also used 1/3 cup of reduced sugar brown sugar. I increased the spices to 1/2 tsp each and kept the lemon at 2 tablespoons. I mixed together the sugar, spices, canned peaches drained and the lemon juice and poured that on top of the chicken. I followed the instructions to baste often with the pan juices, and the result was that the spices stuck to the chicken! After cooking for half an hour, I broiled the whole for three minutes then removed the chicken and peaches to make the sauce. I used 1/2 cup of water and 1 tablespoon of cornstarch. Divided the sauce between the two of us. The chicken was amazingly tender, and the sauce was divine! A keeper for sure!

I did this, but a bit different. Put all the ingredients together and marinated the chicken tenders for about an hour (added olive oil and chicken broth). Tossed them on the grill with the peaches and other veg for a nice dinner. Turned out so good! Sprinkled a little more brown sugar for a caramelization on the chicken as they grilled. Same recipe, just on the grill!

Excellent. I made this dish the other day. I found that by cutting the chicken (2 breast’s butterfly style) salt and pepper both sides and frying it until brown on 1 side, made the chicken look better, didn’t look boiled! I mixed peach juice (in its own juice) with slightly more then 1/4 cup brown sugar, ginger, cloves and about 1 teaspoon of apple cider vinegar and about 1 1/2 teaspoons of chili sauce in a bowl so that it was all incorporated. Placed the peaches on top of the chicken and poured the mixture over the top. Broiled this for 8-10 minutes so the peaches were slightly brown and the chicken cooked through, served with rice with a drizzle of the peach sauce. Loved it!

I used this as a base, and it was fantastic. Had boneless chicken thighs. Dredged in seasoned flour (salt, pepper, onion & garlic powders), and browned in olive oil in skillet. Moved chicken to plate, added a little more olive oil and some of the seasoned flour to make a roux. Dumped in a can of peaches with juice and another 2-3 fresh peaches sliced. Added brown sugar, ginger, cloves, splash of white vinegar (no lemon juice on hand) and chicken stock. Brought to boil so that it started to thicken, then returned chicken to skilled and put in oven at 350 for about 15-20 mins. Served over Basmati rice.

Heeding the other reviews that stated the chicken was too bland, I made a few changes. I cut four raw chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces and put them in a skillet, along with 8 canned peach halves (syrup drained and set aside). I mixed 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1/8 tsp ground ginger, 1/8 tsp ground cloves, and 2 tbsp lemon juice in a bowl, then added the peach syrup to taste (until the main flavor was peach and not lemon). I poured the mixture into the skillet with the chicken and peaches and simmered it on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the chicken was done. The result was delicious--not too sweet, not too sour, and definitely not bland!

This recipe was awesome!! I did use a few of the other recommendations that I feel made the recipe even more of a hit. I soaked the chicken in white wine vinegar and the juice from 1 lemon. Then added garlic powder, onion powder, salt pepper and a hint of cinnamon. I also doubled the amount of other spices used, and I am sooooo glad I did. I made a mix of light brown sugar, ginger, pinch of cinnamon and used all spice instead of cloves( they were out of cloves). I used can peaches in heavy syrup. I coated peaches in my brown sugar mix before putting them on chicken. Once dish was done, I took cooked peaches and chopped up and added to white rice as a side dish. All the let over sauce was poured into rice as well. My kids absolutely loved this and it definitely be in the rotation of meals in our house.

Super simple, fast, and tasty. I kept returning to read the recipe certain that I must have left out a step. But no, it's that easy and fast. I took another reviewer's recommendation to marinate the chicken in white wine vinegar and lemon juice before I browned the breasts in a skillet. After baking I was easily able to thicken the gravy with the corn starch solution. We are not big on sweet flavors and this dish was not overly sweet. I used an entire bag of frozen peaches, too. I am getting requests to make it again!

Delicious!! 
Decreased the sugar, for our tastes 1/2 cup brown sugar is lots. 
My hubby isn't a fan of cloves so I used cinnamon instead. 
1.5 c of frozen peaches from last summers fruit crop. 
Chicken thighs as that's what I had in the freezer. 
Next time I would cook the chicken 10 minutes then drain the grease before adding sugar and peaches. 
Will be making this again!

I browned the chicken in olive oil first and seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic. (Next time, I would be careful if I did this so as not to overcook the chicken.) Then, I mixed the brown sugar, peaches, seasonings and lemon juice all together and poured the mixture over the chicken - made the easy recipe even easier. I also deglazed the skillet that I browned the meat in with a little chicken stock and added that liquid to the peaches mixture as well. Served the chicken with yellow rice.

This recipe doesn’t work essentially! Because the chicken isn’t seasoned enough. On my second attempt I increased ginger to 1/2 teaspoon , and added 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon instead of cloves. And a good pinch of flaked sea salt over the chicken. Before adding the remaining ingredients. We found far more enjoyable.

I made this with Splenda brown sugar, and followed the recipe as is. The chicken was subtly sweet in the best way. I served it with white rice on the side, and some of my peaches got mixed in with the rice, and it was an incredibly amazing combination.

Wow this recipe flavor really packs a punch! I love the simplicity of few ingredients and easy of cooking for a quick dinner meal. I did add a sprinkle of paprika on the chicken before putting in the oven as I am not a fan of baked chicken that isn’t browned first. Sometimes it has that gray-white color so I have found that paprika can help with this. If you love the bold flavors of ginger and cloves together this recipe is for you!!

My family liked the peaches and chicken combo. The sweet and savory flavors were something I never tasted. I did add a few seasonings, paparika, onion powder, and garlic power. I also added rice to the mix.

How wonderful - and different! - to have a sweet main dish that's only 248 calories! I started making this dish some time ago, and it has become a real family favourite. I probably make it about once a month, and for special occasions when hosting family and friends. This dish never fails to earn compliments. Thank you!

I do like I usually do. I change a recipe up a little bit to make it my own instead of using the spices recommended. I used some spicy chicken seasoning gave that sweet and spicy then took it out of the oven and smoked it on my smoker for 20 minutes to give it that smoky flavor
It was great, I only used 2 Tablespoons of sugar and a can of peaches. The spices gave a delicious flavor.
Came out great!
I made an oopsie made the 8 servings with only 3 chicken breast but I used the excess juice on mashed potatoes and dang it's good.

Oh my! I loved this dish! I used 2 chicken breasts, 2 peaches, 3 T brown sugar, 1 1/2 tsp lemon juice, plus a sprinkle of cloves and ginger. It was perfect! I served it over jasmine rice and thickened the pan drippings with the cornstarch/water mixture (just enough of it until thickened). This is definitely a keeper.
